items.title: Dick Katz interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 7, 2002
items.q: muted trumpet, Jonah Jones and so on

ctx.x: Who was taking your place do you know?

I don’t know probably Horace Silver or somebody. I don’t know. He broke the piano. I remember one night Horace broke the piano. It was a little spinet and — oh he was playing opposite me, that’s right — and all the hammers had been knocked off — it was a mess. I loved Horace, I thought he was great. And then I used to work in the Embers. One night I got a — Hank Jones, one of my all time heroes, he’s incredible, he was so in demand that he would take, say yes to three jobs and then at the last minute he’d decide…
